title: Least recently used cache replay
prompt:
Repair solve(payload). Input has capacity (nonnegative integer) and operations. Each operation is
{"op":"put","key":string,"value":JSON_value} or {"op":"get","key":string}. A successful get and
every put make that key most recently used; a miss leaves order unchanged. Updating an existing key
replaces its value. After a put, evict least recently used keys until capacity is respected. Capacity
zero stores nothing. Return {"gets": results_of_gets_in_order, "items": [[key,value],...]} with final
items ordered least to most recently used. A missing get returns null; stored null is still a hit
and updates recency. All JSON values, including false, empty lists and objects, are valid values.

Do not mutate the input. Use only Python's standard library.

Public examples:
- Input: `{"capacity": 1, "operations": [{"op": "put", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "put", "key": "b", "value": 2}, {"op": "get", "key": "a"}, {"op": "get", "key": "b"}]}`; output: `{"gets": [null, 2], "items": [["b", 2]]}`.
- Input: `{"capacity": 2, "operations": []}`; output: `{"gets": [], "items": []}`.

files.public_tests.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
import copy
import json
import unittest
from solution import solve

CASES = json.loads('[{"name": "eviction", "input": {"capacity": 1, "operations": [{"op": "put", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "put", "key": "b", "value": 2}, {"op": "get", "key": "a"}, {"op": "get", "key": "b"}]}, "expected": {"gets": [null, 2], "items": [["b", 2]]}}, {"name": "empty", "input": {"capacity": 2, "operations": []}, "expected": {"gets": [], "items": []}}]')

class PublicExamples(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_examples(self):
        for item in CASES:
            with self.subTest(name=item["name"]):
                value = copy.deepcopy(item["input"])
                self.assertEqual(solve(value), item["expected"])
                self.assertEqual(value, item["input"], "solve must not mutate its input")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
